notes:
Account: Orbitalscribe Archives (large audiovisual archive + transcripts). Heavy long-doc workload (books, broadcast transcripts, logs).

Top-level: they need a two-stage RAG pipeline: dense retrieval (embeddings) + cross-encoder reranker. Primary pain: recall/latency tradeoff and cost-per-query at scale.

Key numbers / constraints (customer-provided):
- Corpus: ~1.2M title-level items, estimated 12M logical chunks after chunking (avg doc length 20k-50k tokens).
- Target QPS: steady 10-20 QPS, spikes to 60 QPS during peak archival queries.
- SLA: p95 end-to-end search latency <= 350ms for interactive UX; p95 reranker step target <120ms.
- Cost target: <= $0.03 per user query (all-in).

Indexing / chunking discussion notes:
- Prefer semantic-aware chunking: paragraph / scene boundaries where possible, otherwise sliding-window 3k token chunks with 200 token overlap for context.
- Want preservation of temporal metadata (broadcast timestamp) and speaker attribution in chunk metadata.
- Interested in adaptive chunk coalescing for short result reassembly (group adjacent chunks at retrieval time).
- Concern: naive 512-token chunking explodes N and harms ANN recall & cost.

Retrieval + reranking architecture preferences:
- Two-stage pipeline: FAISS-style ANN for top-200 candidates -> cross-encoder rerank top-8-16.
- Considering FAISS IVF-PQ or HNSW with quantization for 12M+ vectors; evaluating Pinecone/Milvus hosted vs self-hosted Dedicated.
- Strong preference to keep reranker on GPU (Dedicated/GPU pool). Want batching and KV caching to reduce per-query GPU cost.
- Reranker model experiments: distilled cross-encoder (custom fine-tune on internal QA pairs) vs off-the-shelf cross-encoders. Tradeoff: smaller cross-encoder faster but lower rerank recall.

Evaluation/POC plan and milestones (agreed):
- Phase 0: sample ingest (50k long-docs -> ~400k chunks) to validate chunking heuristics. Metrics: recall@10, MRR, end-to-end p95. (Due: 2026-03-31)
- Phase 1: scale test ingest (1M docs subset) + latency profiling on Dedicated GPU pool. Measure embedding generation throughput and ANN build time. (Due: 2026-04-21)
- Phase 2: cost modeling + canary with live traffic mirror; finalize routing/fallback policies. (Due: 2026-05-15)

POC success criteria (customer-specified):
- recall@10 >= 0.85 on curated eval set
- end-to-end p95 <= 350ms at 20 QPS
- cost per query <= $0.03 at 20 QPS (including embeddings + reranker compute + ANN ops)

Quotes / call snippets:
- CTO: "We can't accept >$0.03 per query at our scale — that kills the business case."
- Search lead: "Chunking is the secret sauce here. If we over-chunk we'll pay for it forever."

Technical open questions / engineering asks for Redwood team:
- Recommendations on chunk size vs recall tradeoff for long transcripts (3k tokens w/ 200 overlap baseline suggested).
- Best-practice for ANN index selection given 12M vectors and p95 <100ms retrieval goal.
- Reranker batching guidance and expected p95 for top-8 cross-encoder on a Dedicated T4/V100 equivalent.
- Template for cost model: tokenized embedding compute + GPU rerank per-call + ANN ops.

Internal POC notes (from AE/SE):
- SE to produce 2 alternative cost projections (hosted vs Dedicated) and 3 reranker model configs (large cross-encoder, distilled, and hybrid rescoring).
- Capture example eval queries from their editorial team (shared in Drive).
- Legal loop initiated for EU residency; affects timeline if Private deployment required.
